```{r setup, eval=FALSE}

library(here)
#library(lubridate)
#library(Unicode) 
library(dplyr)
#library(tidyverse)
library(tibble)
library(pharmaverseadam) # for testing

# to generate test dataset
source(here("R", "nonstd_ascii_dataset_generator.R"))

# to identify rows in your vector that contain unicode characters (by category)
source(here("R", "find_by_uni_category.R"))

source(here("R", "replace_by_category.R"))

source(here("R", "replace_by_codepoint.R"))
#source(here("R", "replace_by_codepoint_old.R"))
```


```{r get_test_data, eval=FALSE}

# Generate 100 records of dirty data
cm_test <- nonstd_ascii_dataset_generator(n=100)

# this is the name of the column vector that we want to clean.
col0 <- cm_test$CMCAT


# This is clean data
aeterm <- pharmaverseadam::adae |> select(AETERM)
```

```{r review_and_report}

#-----------IDENTIFY and REVIEW------------------------------------

# We are looking for the following categories of characters:
# Cc  Control
# Cf  Format (zero-width, BOM, etc.)
# Zs  Non-standard spaces
# Co  Private-use characters
# Cn  Unassigned code points

# initialize a storage list
result <- list()

catlist <- c("Cc", "Cf", "Zs", "Co", "Cn")

# Find the rows in your vector that contain unicode characters by category.
# Get the results and store them in a list named "result"
for (cat in catlist) {
   result[[cat]] <- find_by_uni_category(col0, cat, printsum=TRUE)
}

# The above does the following, but more efficiently:
#result[['Cc']] <- find_by_uni_category(col0, "Cc", printdetails = FALSE) 
#result[['Cf']] <- find_by_uni_category(col0, "Cf", printsum=TRUE)
#result[['Zs']] <-find_by_uni_category(col0, "Zs")
#result[['Co']] <-find_by_uni_category(col0, "Co")
#result[['Cn']] <-find_by_uni_category(col0, "Cn")

```

```{r remove_chars_one_category}

# -----------REMOVE-----------------------------------------
# Eg, for control characters, we probably want to just remove them all.

# Across all character columns in cm_test:

# default, replaces control characters with null 
cm_cleaned_control_a <- replace_by_category(cm_test, "Cc") #default replaces with null 

# replace control characters with a string "12345"
cm_cleaned_control_b <- replace_by_category(cm_test, "Cc", repl="12345")
```

```{r remove_chars_multiple_categories}
# To clean your data for multiple categories:

catlist <- c("Cc", "Cf", "Zs", "Co", "Cn")

# Find the rows in your vector that contain unicode characters by category.
cm_cleaned_combo <- cm_test

for (cat in catlist) {
  cm_cleaned_combo <- replace_by_category(
    cm_cleaned_combo,
    category = cat,
    repl = "@"
 )
}


```


# User-specified character replacement

```{r user_spec_replacement1}
# First define a replacement table (EXAMPLE)
replacement_table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~old_unicode, ~old_name, ~new_unicode, ~new_value, ~action,
  "U+0000", "NULL (NUL)", "", "", "Remove NULL character",
  "U+0009", "HORIZONTAL TAB (TAB)", "U+0020", "SPACE", "Replace TAB with SPACE",
  "U+000A", "LINE FEED (LF)", "U+0020", "SPACE", "Replace LINE FEED with SPACE",
  "U+000D", "CARRIAGE RETURN (CR)", "U+0020", "SPACE", "Replace CARRIAGE RETURN with SPACE",
   "U+200B", "ZERO WIDTH SPACE", "", "", "Remove ZERO WIDTH SPACE" ,
   "U+200C", "ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER", "", "", "Remove ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER" ,
   "U+200D", "ZERO WIDTH JOINER", "", "", "Remove ZERO WIDTH JOINER" ,
  # "U+FEFF", "BYTE ORDER MARK (BOM)", "", "", "Remove BYTE ORDER MARK" ,   # this BOM is a pain to manage
  "U+00A0", "NO-BREAK SPACE", "U+0020", "SPACE", "Replace NO-BREAK SPACE with SPACE",
  "U+2002", "EN SPACE", "U+0020", "SPACE", "Replace EN SPACE with SPACE",
  "U+2003", "EM SPACE", "U+0020", "SPACE", "Replace EM SPACE with SPACE",
  "U+2018", "LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK", "U+0027", "APOSTROPHE", "Replace LEFT SINGLE QUOTE with APOSTROPHE",
  "U+2019", "RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK", "U+0027", "APOSTROPHE", "Replace RIGHT SINGLE QUOTE with APOSTROPHE",
  "U+201C", "LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK", "U+0022", "QUOTATION MARK", "Replace LEFT DOUBLE QUOTE with QUOTATION MARK",
  "U+201D", "RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK", "U+0022", "QUOTATION MARK", "Replace RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTE with QUOTATION MARK",
  "U+2013", "EN DASH", "U+002D", "HYPHEN-MINUS", "Replace EN DASH with HYPHEN-MINUS",
  "U+2014", "EM DASH", "U+002D", "HYPHEN-MINUS", "Replace EM DASH with HYPHEN-MINUS",
  "U+2026", "HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS", "U+002E", "PERIOD", "Replace ELLIPSIS with PERIOD"
)

#print(replacement_table)



# execute the replacement, operates on one column (vector) within a dataframe
# col0_clean <- replace_by_codepoint_old(
#   col0, # like adcm$CMTRT
#   replacement_table1
# )

col0_clean <- replace_by_codepoint(
  col0, # like adcm$CMTRT
  replacement_table1
)



# PROGRAMMERS NOTE:: 
# The codepoint U+FEFF (\ufeff, a.k.a. byte order mark (BOM)) is replaced with null ("") by design. 
# This is because the BOM causes a warning for empty search pattern in this workflow.
# Try this for example of warning:
# stringi::stri_replace_all_fixed(
#   "ABC",
#   "\ufeff",
#   ""
# )


```

```{r user_spec_replacement2}

# Another example replacement table for things we want to remove/replace in our data.
# This replacement table example below shows that we can identify codepoints that are multi-byte sequences (when encoded in 
# UTF-8) - like the vulgar 1/4 - and replace them with a multi-character replacement - like "1/4".
#
# Note that some are text strings like "ASCII TEXT" or "ASTERISK" which are a bit silly but good for illustrative purposes.

replacement_table2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~old_unicode, ~old_name, ~new_unicode, ~new_value, ~action,

  # SMART SINGLE QUOTES
  "U+2018", "LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK", "U+0027", "APOSTROPHE",
  "Replace smart quote with apostrophe",
  "U+2019", "RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK", "U+0027", "APOSTROPHE",
  "Replace smart quote with apostrophe",
  "U+201B", "SINGLE HIGH-REVERSED-9 QUOTATION MARK", "U+0027", "APOSTROPHE",
  "Replace quote with apostrophe",

  # SMART DOUBLE QUOTES
  "U+201C", "LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK", "U+0022", "QUOTATION MARK",
  "Replace smart quote with quote",
  "U+201D", "RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK", "U+0022", "QUOTATION MARK",
  "Replace smart quote with quote",

  # DASHES
  "U+2010", "HYPHEN", "U+002D", "HYPHEN-MINUS",
  "Normalize hyphen",
  "U+2011", "NON-BREAKING HYPHEN", "U+002D", "HYPHEN-MINUS",
  "Normalize hyphen",
  "U+2012", "FIGURE DASH", "U+002D", "HYPHEN-MINUS",
  "Normalize dash",
  "U+2013", "EN DASH", "U+002D", "HYPHEN-MINUS",
  "Normalize dash",
  "U+2014", "EM DASH", "U+002D", "HYPHEN-MINUS",
  "Normalize dash",
  "U+2212", "MINUS SIGN", "U+002D", "HYPHEN-MINUS",
  "Normalize minus sign",

  # ELLIPSIS
  "U+2026", "HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS", "U+002E", "PERIOD",
  "Replace ellipsis with period",

  # BULLETS
  "U+2022", "BULLET", "U+002A", "ASTERISK",
  "Replace bullet with asterisk",
  "U+25CF", "BLACK CIRCLE", "U+002A", "ASTERISK",
  "Replace bullet with asterisk",

  # FRACTIONS ----> This is where new_value is needed, where we replace not with unicode but with text string like "1/2"
  "U+00BC", "VULGAR FRACTION ONE QUARTER", "1/4", "ASCII TEXT","Normalize fraction",
  "U+00BD", "VULGAR FRACTION ONE HALF", "1/2", "ASCII TEXT","Normalize fraction",
  "U+00BE", "VULGAR FRACTION THREE QUARTERS", "3/4", "ASCII TEXT","Normalize fraction",

  # TRADEMARKS / COPYRIGHTS 
  "U+00A9", "COPYRIGHT SIGN", "(C)", "ASCII TEXT",
  "Normalize copyright",
  "U+00AE", "REGISTERED SIGN", "(R)", "ASCII TEXT",
  "Normalize registered mark",
  "U+2122", "TRADE MARK SIGN", "(TM)", "ASCII TEXT",
  "Normalize trademark"
)


#execute the replacement over all the character columns in a dataframe
cm_clean <- cm_test %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.character),
      ~ replace_by_codepoint(.x, replacement_table2)
    )
  )


# Some values in cm_test$CMCAT are getting replaced entirely with null!

x <- "ANALGESICS©¶≈"

check_this <- replace_by_codepoint(x, replacement_table2)



```





# Overview 

Welcome to `charwash()`!\above

`charwash()` reviews the content of character columns within your dataframe and returns information about the non-standard ascii characters within (if any).



# Support

Support is provided via [pharmaverse Slack](https://pharmaverse.slack.com/).
